prompt:
A broadcast quality control desk photographed square on. A player monitor stands paused with its timecode window filling most of the screen in large even-width figures, and a printed continuity check sheet lies on the desk under it, angled toward the camera and legible.

The check sheet has a heading strip that reads 29.97 DROP FRAME, and under it two columns headed LAST FRAME and NEXT FRAME, four rows deep. The four entries in the LAST FRAME column are already there, one to a row and in this order:
01:08:59;29
01:09:59;29
01:19:59;29
01:10:14;15
The NEXT FRAME column is empty and is the job.

The monitor is paused on the very next frame after the first row's last frame, and its window carries that frame's timecode.

How this station's timecode counts is a matter of the broadcast standard the desk works to; I am deliberately not writing that standard out and I am deliberately not telling you any of the four answers. Fill the NEXT FRAME column from the standard.

There is nothing else on the sheet: no working, no note about the frame rate, no fifth row, no arrows.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a screen displaying a row of figures separated by punctuation, with a printed sheet of figures lying below it? A photograph, a screenshot or an illustration ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image shows a blank card that just states an answer, or shows neither a screen nor a sheet. Answer yes or no only.
